sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining with anti-HA antibody confirmed the tag is accessible on the extracellular face of the plasma membrane. Construct was used to study GluD1 surface trafficking and synapse formation in the context of neurexin/Cbln1 interactions; surface expression was confirmed. Receptor function per se (ion channel gating) was NOT MEASURED with this tagged construct.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly names residues 20 and 21 as the flanking positions of the HA insert, confirmed by Python lookup: seq[19]='A' (residue 20, last of SP) and seq[20]='D' (residue 21, first of mature extracellular domain). The tag is therefore at the extracellular N-terminus of the mature protein, 541 residues from the nearest TM helix — no steric or topological concern. L2 (same paper, same construct, GSA linker detail) and L3 (human GRID1, beta-lactamase at the identical SP/ATD junction) independently corroborate this junction; because all three pin the same residue-level position, this is one site grounded in L1 as the most explicit source. Full-length mouse GluD1 expressed in neurons/HEK cells; HA tag (with TR linker, full insert TRYPYDVPDYA) placed between residues 20 and 21 — explicitly stated as 'between amino acids 20 and 21' in the construct description. The same junction is independently confirmed by L2 (GSA-linked HA after the signal peptide of the same construct) and by L3 (beta-lactamase fused in-frame between the signal peptide and the amino-terminal domain of human GRID1 in pCI-Neo). Residue 20 (A) is the last residue of the signal peptide (SP: 1–20); residue 21 (D) is the first residue of the mature extracellular N-terminus (extracellular span: 21–561), placing the tag 541 residues from the first TM boundary (562).

sources.claim: The cDNAs of the following genes were used: mouse grid1 (GenBank 14803) in pcDNA3 for GluD1 with an HA tag inserted at the N terminus between amino acids 20 and 21 (20-TRYPYDVPDYA-21); mouse grid2 (GenBank 14804) for GluD2 in pcDNA3; Nrxn1 as Nrx1bS4(+)S5(−)-3xFLAG in pCAGGS; Cbln1 as Myc-Cbln1 in pCAG; WT EGFP in pcDNA3.

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) converge on the single junction after residue 20 (last of signal peptide) / before residue 21 (first of mature extracellular ATD). L1 and L2 are from the same paper (PMC11295041) and describe the same mouse GluD1-HA construct; L3 (PMC10840383) independently uses the identical SP/ATD junction for a beta-lactamase fusion in human GRID1. Because they all pin the same junction, this is one site, not three. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion, any C-terminal tag, or any intracellular tag for GRID1. The second extracellular span (659–830) has no ledger support and is not proposed.
